Flags (ISO country/subdivision code, e.g. "fr", "de", "gb-eng")
Controls period labelling and the halftime→ET audio cue. Leave unticked for a normal match — the second half (including any stoppage time) will always be labelled "2ND HALF" regardless of how many added minutes it runs to.
Match duration is worked out automatically from whichever data goes latest — the momentum timeline, a stoppage-time goal, or an ambient audio window. If none of those reflect genuine injury time with no goal in it (e.g. a scoreless stoppage period), add a max_minute row to the Meta CSV with the true final minute to override it directly.
Data format
FotMob matchDetails response (paste full JSON)
From fotmob.com: open a match → DevTools (F12) → Network tab → reload → find the matchDetails request → right-click it → Copy → Copy response (this avoids partial/truncated copies) → paste the whole thing here.

Timeline (the momentum curve) is reliably extracted — confirmed against real match data. Events (goals) and team colours are best-effort — I haven't confirmed FotMob's exact field names for those yet, so check the preview against what you know actually happened before using the result. Team names are used if found; colours are left alone if not found, rather than guessed.
Match info CSV — key, value
Team names/colours, competition, date, venue — everything needed to set up a match, in one editable, spreadsheet-friendly file. Edit this directly to build a match from scratch (e.g. a school or local game) without touching the fields above.
Timeline CSV — minute, value (−1 to 1)
Events CSV — minute, team (home/away), label, photo, audio (optional)
"team" must be exactly "home" or "away" — it maps to whichever colour/name you've set above, not the literal team name. "photo" is optional — a direct image URL to show in the goal pop-up. "audio" is optional — a short commentary clip that plays instead of the crowd roar for that specific goal, with the match automatically slowing down for its full length; attach one using the picker above rather than editing the CSV cell directly, since clips are stored as long embedded text.
Lineups CSV — team, role (starter/sub), number, name, club, age
Match data (JSON)
timeline: [minute, value] pairs, value from −1 (away threatening) to 1 (home threatening). events: goals with minute + team ('home'/'away') + optional label + optional photo (image URL).
Link type
View only opens straight into playback with no access to the Data & teams panel at all — this is what most recipients want, and is the default. Fully configurable opens the normal editable app with this match already loaded, for someone you want to be able to tweak it themselves.
Share link
Creates a short Gist-backed link (via the same gist-proxy Worker as the Geo Mapper apps, called at its full URL since this app isn't served behind that Worker's path-based proxy route). The exact request path is modelled closely on Geo Mapper's own working create/update logic, but hasn't been confirmed end-to-end against the live Worker from this app yet — if it fails, this automatically falls back to a longer link with the match compressed directly into the URL, which needs no Worker at all. Once a Gist link has been created in this browser tab, clicking the button again updates that same link rather than making a new one — so you can keep editing the match and the one link you already sent out will show the latest version. The compressed fallback link can't be updated this way; a change means a new link.
Load a share link
Opening a share link directly in the browser loads it automatically — this box is only for pasting one in manually.
